question.problem: Given that the function $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)-3{x}^{2}$ has a critical point in the interval $[0,0.5],$ use the Newton-Raphson process for optimization starting from ${x}_{0}=0.5$ to estimate the critical point. Round your final answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}{{f}^{″}({x}_{n})},
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ and ${f}^{″}({x}_{n})$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n},$ respectively.

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)-3{x}^{2})^{′}=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-6x=2(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-3x), \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-6x)^{′}=-16\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)-6=-2(8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{2(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}_{n})-3{x}_{n})}{-2(8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4{x}_{n})+3)} \\  & ={x}_{n}+\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}_{n})-3{x}_{n}}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4{x}_{n})+3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=0.5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}_{0})-3{x}_{0}}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4{x}_{0})+3} \\  & =0.5+\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot 0.5)-3\cdot 0.5}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 0.5)+3} \\  & =0.272\,999….\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}+\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}_{1})-3{x}_{1}}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4{x}_{1})+3} \\  & =0.272\,999…+\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot 0.272\,999…)-3\cdot 0.272\,999…}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 0.272\,999…)+3} \\  & =0.283\,140…., \\ {x}_{3} & ={x}_{2}+\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}_{2})-3{x}_{2}}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4{x}_{2})+3} \\  & =0.283\,140…+\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot 0.283\,140…)-3\cdot 0.283\,140…}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 0.283\,140…)+3} \\  & =0.283\,068….\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the last two approximations ${x}_{2}≈0.28$ and ${x}_{3}≈0.28$ are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the critical point of the function is $x≈0.28,$ rounded to two decimal places.
